- When sentiment is consistently negative over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–2% relative to prior period.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >5% from prior day), model often overshoots in next 3–5 days; apply downward correction of 1–3% for 3–7 day horizon.
- If sentiment flips from negative to positive mid-horizon, model fails to adjust; re-estimate mean reversion toward recent 7-day average if sentiment shifts.
- Model underestimates when sentiment is positive and price is trending upward; increase forecast by 0.5–1.5% for 3–7 day horizon if sentiment >0.
- For 30-day horizon, model consistently underestimates true price by 1–3% when sentiment is negative; apply upward bias of 1–2% if sentiment <0.
- If sentiment is mixed or neutral, model tends to lag; forecast should be adjusted upward by 0.5–1.5% for 3–7 day horizon to catch momentum.
